@vikramsg check this out:

Plan mode injects this hardcoded reminder that you can't turn off from config:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts#L388-L410

The actual reminder is here:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/plan.txt#L1-L9

It literally starts with:

```text
<system-reminder>
# Plan Mode - System Reminder

CRITICAL: Plan mode ACTIVE - you are in READ-ONLY phase.
```

Then switching back to build is also just another hardcoded `<system-reminder>`:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/build-switch.txt#L1-L5

And the newer experimental plan mode path hardcodes an even bigger inline reminder here:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts#L441-L510

### What it means

So, you can configure a 100% identical primary agent to Plan's prompts, same permissions, but it will not behave the same as the special internal Plan mode.

Similarly, if you want to extend plan mode to maybe persist its plans into source control or something or sync them to a company Obsidian vault, it's extremely hard because you are constantly fighting this read only directive (learned this the hard way)

Related issue found: bare URLs in markdown (not just tables) are rendered as `url (url)` due to `MarkdownRenderable` in `@opentui/core`.

**Root cause:** The `"link"` case in `renderInlineToken` unconditionally appends ` (href)` when `conceal=true` (the default). For bare/autolinked URLs, the link text equals the href, producing duplication like `https://example.com (https://example.com)`.

**Fix:** Skip the `(href)` suffix when `linkText === token.href`. Filed upstream: https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/1050

This affects all bare URLs in rendered markdown, but is most visible in tables where column width is limited.

### Possibly related: `opencode mcp auth <name>` fails with opaque "JSON Parse error" when `mcp-auth.json` is corrupted

Hitting this on v1.14.41 (macOS). Different code path from the spawn-ENOENT issue above, but filing here since it's the active MCP-pain thread — happy to split into its own issue if preferred.

**Symptom**
```
$ opencode mcp auth gitlab-mcp
┌  MCP OAuth Authentication
Error: Unexpected error, check log file at /Users/me/.local/share/opencode/log/2026-05-11T160949.log for more details

JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string
```

The log file contains only the standard config-loading lines and stops before any actionable error — nothing identifies the offending file.

**Root cause**
`~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json` was corrupted with a stray extra `}` at EOF:
```
...
  }
}
}   ← extra
```
`JSON.parse` rejects this with `Extra data` (the underlying message that gets swallowed into the generic "Unable to parse JSON string"). Fix was to strip the trailing brace and re-serialize — `opencode mcp auth` then works.

**Two suggestions**

1. **Surface the file path in the error.** Wrapping the `JSON.parse` on the auth store with a try/catch that re-throws with the path would have made this a 10-second fix instead of a log-dive. Something like:
   ```
   Failed to parse /Users/me/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json: Extra data at position 7110
   ```

2. **Write `mcp-auth.json` atomically.** A trailing extra `}` strongly suggests a non-atomic write (write-in-place with a previous longer payload not fully overwritten, or an interrupted write merging with stale tail). Standard tmp-file + `rename(2)` pattern would prevent this entire failure mode.

Let me know if you'd like a separate issue for this — the symptom (`opencode mcp auth` rather than runtime MCP spawning) is genuinely distinct from the original report, even though both live in the MCP subsystem.

I investigated this from the OpenCode binary and MCP protocol level. The core issue is that **Google's MCP servers don't expose OAuth discovery**, so OpenCode has no way to initiate the OAuth flow.

### How OAuth works for servers that DO work (e.g., Slack)

Slack exposes `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` at its MCP URL:

```
$ curl https://mcp.slack.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
{
  "issuer": "https://slack.com",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access",
  ...
}
```

OpenCode discovers this → constructs the authorization URL → opens browser → user consents → callback delivers code → token exchange completes. This flow works reliably.

### Why Google MCP servers fail

Google's MCP endpoints return 404 for OAuth discovery:

```
$ curl https://people.googleapis.com/mcp/v1/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
404 Not Found

$ curl https://people.googleapis.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
404 Not Found
```

Additionally, Google's servers respond 200 to `initialize` and `tools/list` **without any authentication**. Auth is only enforced on `tools/call`. So OpenCode:
1. Connects via StreamableHTTP → 200 OK
2. Lists tools → gets toolCount (e.g., 3 for People, 10 for Gmail)
3. Considers the connection "successful" → reports "Authentication successful!"
4. Never triggers OAuth because the server never challenged it

### What OpenCode has available but doesn't use

The `opencode.json` config already has the OAuth client config:

```json
"google-people": {
  "type": "remote",
  "url": "https://people.googleapis.com/mcp/v1",
  "oauth": {
    "clientId": "...",
    "clientSecret": "...",
    "scope": "..."
  }
}
```

### Proposed fix

When a server doesn't expose `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` but the config has an `oauth` block with `clientId`/`clientSecret`/`scope`, OpenCode should fall back to **client-side OAuth configuration** using Google's standard endpoints:
- Authorization: `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`
- Token: `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`

This would also fix BigQuery MCP and any other Google MCP server.

### Confirmed working services (once tokens are manually injected)

Using manually obtained tokens written to `mcp-auth.json`, all Google MCP servers work:
- ✅ People (3 tools)
- ✅ Gmail (10 tools)  
- ✅ Calendar (8 tools)
- ✅ Drive (8 tools)

### Environment
- OpenCode 1.14.48
- macOS 15.5 (darwin/arm64)
- Google Workspace MCP (Developer Preview)

Hey @Sanjay-doppalapudi — nice work on this, we hit the exact same issue with Google's MCP servers and independently filed #26912 to fix it.

Our PRs overlap on the core problem: `connect()` succeeds without auth, so the SDK never triggers OAuth. Your forced `auth()` call in `startAuth()` addresses that well.

However, there's a second problem that affects Google specifically: after forcing `auth()`, the SDK calls `discoverOAuthMetadata()` which does a `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` against the MCP server URL (e.g. `googleapis.com`). Google doesn't implement RFC 8414 discovery, so that fetch fails and the OAuth flow still doesn't complete.

Our PR (#26912) addresses both:
1. The same auth-trigger fix (forcing `auth()` when no tokens exist)
2. A `discoveryState()` / `saveDiscoveryState()` implementation on `McpOAuthProvider` that lets users specify `authorizationEndpoint` and `tokenEndpoint` in config — the SDK checks `discoveryState()` before attempting `.well-known` discovery, so it skips the failing fetch entirely

Happy to collaborate on this — we could merge the approaches, or I could rebase our discovery piece on top of yours if the maintainers prefer that structure. Let me know what makes sense.

Hey @yanniznik, 
Good catch on the RFC 8414 discovery issue ,I hadn't hit that in testing since the Google Drive server I was working with was failing earlier in the flow.
Your approach of implementing discoveryState() / saveDiscoveryState() on McpOAuthProvider with configurable authorizationEndpoint and tokenEndpoint seems like the right way to handle servers that don't support .well-known discovery. The SDK checks discoveryState() first, so if we save the endpoints there, it skips the failing fetch.
I think the cleanest path is:
